dispatch: W6 Emergency Panel — FlowAI self-testing capability (2026-05-20)

documentedDuplicates.meta-llama: Slot 3 (llama-3.3-70b-instruct, post-Gemini-demote 2026-05-16) + Slot 9 (llama-4-maverick). Different generations, different serving paths on OpenRouter, independent in practice. Documented per W5b dispatch #2 (2026-05-16, commit 556a751 triggering evidence).

allObjections.title: §5 self-application creates infinite regress
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §5 mandates FlowAI applies to its own development, but if FlowAI must improve itself before being considered functional, and it needs to be functional to improve itself, the system enters an unresolvable bootstrap paradox. The spec provides no escape hatch or initial bootstrap mechanism.

allObjections.title: PATH B violates core §1 promise
allObjections.detail: The proposal admits PATH B produces no new URL despite CA-18 §1 explicitly stating 'Output: ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL'. This isn't a minor gap - it's a fundamental violation of the core product definition that the UI actively advertises but cannot deliver.

allObjections.title: No rollback for self-improvement failures
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §5 requires FlowAI to improve its own source tree via §29 Build/Wire Construction Engine, but neither §5 nor the proposal defines what happens when FlowAI damages itself during self-improvement. Unlike external products where both URLs are preserved, self-modification could brick the platform.

allObjections.title: Proof validation relies on deceptive evidence
allObjections.detail: The proposal reveals PATH A testing uses 'Claude-Code-operated CLI scripts' - an external LLM agent manually operating FlowAI, not FlowAI operating itself. This fundamentally misrepresents the product's actual capabilities to stakeholders reviewing proof artifacts.

allObjections.title: Lack of UI
allObjections.detail: The current implementation of FlowAI does not have a functional UI that can complete a full improvement cycle, which contradicts the promise made in CA-18 §1. The UI at `flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai` only accepts URL input and runs a partial audit, but does not generate fixes or deploy a new URL.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The current testing approach relies on CLI scripts invoked through Claude Code agents, which may not be representative of real-world usage and may not exercise the product surface as intended. This could lead to a false sense of security and mask potential issues with the product.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Architecture
allObjections.detail: The existence of two separate paths, PATH A and PATH B, may indicate an inconsistent architecture that could lead to maintenance and scalability issues. The lack of a unified canonical FlowAI Engine that can be invoked by any caller (UI, CLI, API, agent) may cause problems in the long run.

allObjections.title: Incomplete UI Integration
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not address the integration of the Construction Engine with the UI. §10 Self-Audit engine is functional, but there is no mechanism to trigger the Construction Engine from the UI, which is a critical gap.

allObjections.title: Lack of Operator Control
allObjections.detail: The current design lacks operator control over the improvement cycle. Operators cannot initiate or control the construction process from the UI, which contradicts the user agency principle in CA-18 §1.

allObjections.title: Potential for Infinite Self-Loop
allObjections.detail: The proposal suggests prioritizing FlowAI-on-FlowAI improvements, which could lead to an infinite self-loop. This focus may delay the platform's ability to improve external products, limiting its practical utility.

allObjections.title: PATH B audit-only
allObjections.detail: PATH B currently only performs an audit and does not generate a new deployable URL, which contradicts CA-18 §1.

allObjections.title: No UI-driven construction
allObjections.detail: There is no operator-reachable path through the UI to complete a full improvement cycle as required by CA-18 §1.

allObjections.title: Self-application gap
allObjections.detail: FlowAI's self-application to its own development process (CA-18 §5) is not fully realized through the UI, creating a gap in the symbiotic relationship.

allObjections.title: Conflicting definitions of 'product'
allObjections.detail: The document uses 'product' to refer to both FlowAI itself and the external URLs it processes. This ambiguity, especially in J4, makes it difficult to assess whether the 'product' is being adequately tested.

allObjections.title: Unclear 'substantial transformation' metric
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §1 emphasizes 'substantial transformation' as a quality guarantee, but the definition of 'substantial' is subjective and lacks concrete metrics. This makes it difficult to objectively determine whether FlowAI is meeting its promise, especially in self-testing scenarios.

allObjections.title: Risk of over-optimization on self-loop
allObjections.detail: Focusing solely on FlowAI-on-FlowAI (J3) could lead to over-optimization for a narrow use case, potentially neglecting the broader range of inputs and edge cases encountered with external products. This could result in a system that performs well on itself but poorly on real-world applications.

allObjections.title: Lack of rollback strategy for UI wiring
allObjections.detail: Wiring the UI directly to the Construction Engine (J2) without a clear rollback strategy poses a risk. If the integration introduces bugs or instability, it could disrupt the entire FlowAI workflow, including the CLI-based construction path.

allObjections.title: PATH B violates §1 output requirement
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §1 mandates 'Output: ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL' for any input. PATH B's audit-only output without a deployable URL fundamentally fails this core promise. The proposal acknowledges this gap but offers no interim mitigation.

allObjections.title: Self-application failure in §5
allObjections.detail: The absence of UI-path self-improvement violates CA-18 §5's requirement that FlowAI applies to its own development. PATH A's CLI dependency creates a special-case exemption where FlowAI-on-FlowAI requires non-canonical operator intervention, undermining the symbiotic principle.

allObjections.title: Proof validity misrepresentation risk
allObjections.detail: Reporting external product improvements via PATH A while the UI remains broken creates false product readiness signals. This risks stakeholder deception by demonstrating capabilities through non-product-surface mechanisms (Claude Code CLI), contravening honest assessment obligations in §1.

allObjections.title: Architectural fragmentation
allObjections.detail: Maintaining separate PATH A (construction) and PATH B (audit) engines violates §5's symbiotic principle by preventing knowledge transfer between internal and external improvement cycles. Findings from PATH B audits don't feed into PATH A's construction logic, creating disjointed learning loops.

allObjections.title: Audit-only breaks §1 promise
allObjections.detail: In PATH B, the UI accepts a URL but terminates at findings instead of producing a new deployable URL. That directly conflicts with CA-18 §1’s explicit “Output: ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL,” so the UI is not implementing the advertised product promise. The proposal treats this as a gap, but it may actually be a separate product class (audit) mislabeled as improvement.

allObjections.title: Self-loop not proven in UI
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §5 says FlowAI applies to its own development process, including its own UI and source tree. The proposal admits the current self-improvement path is CLI-only via Claude Code, which means the canonical self-application is not reachable through the product surface. That makes the self-reference claim operationally unverified and creates a mismatch between canonical language and user-facing behavior.

allObjections.title: Registry adoption adds hidden coupling
allObjections.detail: The proposed “adopt as product” / product_registry-based path in J2 risks adding manual classification just to make URL improvement possible. That injects operator judgment and schema coupling into what should be a direct URL-in/URL-out flow, increasing the chance of misregistration, stale registry state, and ambiguous provenance for outputs. It also creates a new failure mode where the system can appear to support arbitrary URLs only after a non-obvious manual step.

allObjections.title: PATH B contradicts CA-18 §1
allObjections.detail: The current UI implementation (PATH B) does not produce a new deployable URL, violating the canonical promise of 'any URL in -> new deployable URL out'.

allObjections.title: Lack of self-improvement capability
allObjections.detail: FlowAI cannot improve its own UI through its own UI, contradicting CA-18 §5 which states that FlowAI applies to its own development process.

allObjections.title: CLI workaround is not product-level proof
allObjections.detail: The current testing approach using CLI scripts invoked through Claude Code agents does not exercise the product surface, potentially invalidating the proof that FlowAI works as a product.

allObjections.title: §1 output guarantee unmet by PATH B
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §1 explicitly requires 'ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL' for any input URL, yet PATH B (UI arbitrary-URL submission) only runs §10 Self-Audit and terminates without invoking the §29 Construction Engine or producing a new URL; the audit-only short-circuit directly violates the 'substantial transformation per run' metric.

allObjections.title: §5 self-application lacks UI path
allObjections.detail: CA-18 §5 mandates FlowAI-on-FlowAI via the §29 Build/Wire engine and §11 Clearance Protocol, but the only working path (PATH A) requires Claude-Code CLI invocation outside the operator-facing UI at flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai, collapsing the published 'self-application is canonical operating mode' claim.

allObjections.title: 8-Step Pipeline omits UI wiring
allObjections.detail: The canonical 8-step pipeline (§9) places 'build' (step 3) and 'deploy' (step 5) after research/design, yet no mechanism connects the UI form input to product_registry registration or S1-S8 execution; the Self-Governance Layer (§10) components trigger only on existing registered products, leaving arbitrary-URL flows stranded at audit.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Implementing CA-18 §5's self-improvement mandate without proper safeguards could result in FlowAI corrupting its own codebase during an improvement cycle, leaving the platform non-functional with no automated recovery path - worse than simply having limited functionality.
adversarial.precedent: The Therac-25 radiation therapy machine's software updates introduced lethal bugs because the system lacked proper safeguards when modifying its own operational parameters - similar to FlowAI modifying its own source without defined failure boundaries.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal should be rejected because it attempts to paper over a fundamental architectural flaw with process band-aids. FlowAI's UI cannot deliver its core §1 promise (URL in -> new URL out), and the proposed fixes either require massive architectural changes or perpetuate the current deception of using external LLM agents to simulate functionality. The platform should first be architected to actually work through its own UI before any self-improvement capabilities are considered.

J1.pick_text: Fundamental flaw — PATH B as audit-only contradicts CA-18 §1 ("Output: ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL"). A URL-in path that produces no new URL is not FlowAI by definition; it is a separate audit tool mislabeled as FlowAI. MUST be fixed.
J1.rationale: The specification is unambiguous - 'ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL' leaves no room for audit-only paths to claim compliance with §1.

J2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
J2.rationale: All options assume the Construction Engine is production-ready for arbitrary URLs, but the proposal admits it only works via 'Claude-Code-operated CLI scripts' - none address the fundamental issue that the engine itself may not be ready for UI integration.

J3.pick_text: YES, self-first. §5 explicitly makes FlowAI-on-FlowAI canonical. A platform that cannot improve itself through its own UI has not yet demonstrated the §1 promise; testing external products before the self-test is theatre. Lock external proof until self-loop closes.
J3.rationale: If FlowAI cannot improve itself through its own UI, it has not proven it can improve anything - external tests would be meaningless theater when the core loop is broken.

J4.pick_text: Worse than invalid — actively misleading. Reporting "FlowAI improved product X" when the only invocation path was a Claude-Code-operated CLI builds false expectations among reviewers/stakeholders that the UI works. Either (a) stop calling these runs "FlowAI improvement cycles" until the UI closes the loop, or (b) explicitly mark every artifact "produced via CLI; UI does not yet support this".
J4.rationale: Using an external LLM to manually operate CLI scripts fundamentally misrepresents the product's capabilities - stakeholders believe FlowAI is self-operating when it's actually being puppeted by Claude.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal reveals FlowAI is essentially non-functional as specified in CA-18 §1, relying on external LLM agents to simulate capabilities it doesn't possess through its actual product surface.

objections.detail: CA-18 §5 says FlowAI applies to its own development process, including its own UI and source tree. The proposal admits the current self-improvement path is CLI-only via Claude Code, which means the canonical self-application is not reachable through the product surface. That makes the self-reference claim operationally unverified and creates a mismatch between canonical language and user-facing behavior.

objections.title: Registry adoption adds hidden coupling
objections.detail: The proposed “adopt as product” / product_registry-based path in J2 risks adding manual classification just to make URL improvement possible. That injects operator judgment and schema coupling into what should be a direct URL-in/URL-out flow, increasing the chance of misregistration, stale registry state, and ambiguous provenance for outputs. It also creates a new failure mode where the system can appear to support arbitrary URLs only after a non-obvious manual step.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the UI keeps offering “improve any URL” while only performing audit, users may trust that a deployable improved URL is forthcoming and plan work around it. That is worse than a transparent read-only audit tool, because it creates false confidence and wastes operator time on a workflow that cannot complete.
adversarial.precedent: Aider’s own writeup on code-in-JSON notes that wrapping code in structured JSON can worsen output quality and that plain-text/code-first flows were often better; similarly, forcing an interface promise before the end-to-end path exists can degrade the actual product experience. More broadly, many tools that expose a partial “AI-assisted” workflow before the action loop is closed end up being treated as demos rather than usable products.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring is that the proposal seems to conflate a backend capability with a product capability. Until the UI itself can complete URL-in to new-URL-out, any claim of “FlowAI works” is at best incomplete and at worst misleading. Deferring would preserve honesty, avoid overpromising, and force the team to unify the experience before expanding scope.

J1.pick_text: Fundamental flaw — PATH B as audit-only contradicts CA-18 §1 ("Output: ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL"). A URL-in path that produces no new URL is not FlowAI by definition; it is a separate audit tool mislabeled as FlowAI. MUST be fixed.
J1.rationale: This is the clearest reading of the canonical promise: URL in must yield a new deployable URL out. An audit-only surface cannot satisfy that requirement and therefore cannot stand as a compliant FlowAI path.

J2.pick_text: Wire the UI submit-URL form to the existing Construction Engine (CA-17 S1-S8) end-to-end: URL input -> S1 baseline -> S2-S7 transform -> S8 deploy-to-new-URL, with progress streamed to the UI. No new architecture; activate what already exists per CA-17 + remove the audit-only short-circuit in PATH B.
J2.rationale: This is the minimum change that directly closes the gap described in the proposal without inventing a new product model. It preserves the existing engine while making the UI actually satisfy the canonical flow.

J3.pick_text: Self-first ONLY through a defined milestone (e.g. one full improvement cycle completed against flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai with measurable score delta + new URL deployed), then external products. Avoids indefinite self-loop while honoring §5.
J3.rationale: This best balances the canonical self-application requirement with a practical milestone to prevent endless self-referential work. It establishes a concrete proof gate before external expansion.

J4.pick_text: Worse than invalid — actively misleading. Reporting "FlowAI improved product X" when the only invocation path was a Claude-Code-operated CLI builds false expectations among reviewers/stakeholders that the UI works. Either (a) stop calling these runs "FlowAI improvement cycles" until the UI closes the loop, or (b) explicitly mark every artifact "produced via CLI; UI does not yet support this".
J4.rationale: This goes beyond merely distinguishing engine vs product; it flags the communication risk created by the current evidence. If the UI path fails, presenting CLI runs as product proof is misleading unless carefully labeled.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The main issue is not whether the underlying engines exist, but whether the shipped product fulfills its own published contract. On that standard, the UI-only audit path is insufficient until it can produce a deployable URL end-to-end.

objections.title: §1 output guarantee unmet by PATH B
objections.detail: CA-18 §1 explicitly requires 'ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL' for any input URL, yet PATH B (UI arbitrary-URL submission) only runs §10 Self-Audit and terminates without invoking the §29 Construction Engine or producing a new URL; the audit-only short-circuit directly violates the 'substantial transformation per run' metric.

perReviewer.overallNotes: All objections target explicit mismatches between canonical sections and current PATH A/B implementation.

questions.topic: J1 — Is PATH B (audit-only, no fixes, no new deployable URL) an acceptable design for FlowAI, or a fundamental flaw that must be fixed for FlowAI to deliver its promise per CA-18 §1 ("any URL in -> new deployable URL out, perfected across all 10 quality dimensions per run")?

options.text: Fundamental flaw — PATH B as audit-only contradicts CA-18 §1 ("Output: ALWAYS a new, separate, deployable URL"). A URL-in path that produces no new URL is not FlowAI by definition; it is a separate audit tool mislabeled as FlowAI. MUST be fixed.

Acceptable design — audit-only is a legitimate Mode A (read-only inspection) and the "new URL out" promise applies only when the user explicitly requests construction/improvement. PATH B as audit can coexist with a separate Construct/Improve path.
Flaw but deferrable — PATH B violates §1 in principle but the proof-phase exemption allows shipping audit-only externally while construction matures internally; document the gap and revisit at GA.

Reframe the question — PATH B is fine IF the UI labels it explicitly as "Audit" (a distinct surface from "Improve"); the §1 promise applies to the Improve surface only. Add a labeling fix, not an architectural fix.

questions.topic: J2 — What is the minimum architectural change to enable FlowAI to improve any URL submitted through its own UI (including its own URL flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai), without CLI workarounds — i.e., to satisfy CA-18 §1 end-to-end through the UI?

options.text: Wire the UI submit-URL form to the existing Construction Engine (CA-17 S1-S8) end-to-end: URL input -> S1 baseline -> S2-S7 transform -> S8 deploy-to-new-URL, with progress streamed to the UI. No new architecture; activate what already exists per CA-17 + remove the audit-only short-circuit in PATH B.
Merge PATH A (CLI construction) and PATH B (UI audit) into a single canonical FlowAI Engine that any caller (UI, CLI, API, agent) invokes the same way; PATHs become call-sites, not separate engines.

Add a "submit any URL" canonical entry-point that registers the URL as a new product_registry entry and triggers the standard §11 Six-Step Clearance + §29 Build/Wire flow; UI calls this entry-point. Minimal: it is one new HTTP route + product_registry insert, but reuses every downstream engine.

Provide the operator a UI affordance to migrate any submitted URL into the existing product_registry manually (one-click "adopt as product"), then run the existing construction flow against the adopted product. Cheaper than full URL-in/URL-out automation; preserves operator control.

questions.topic: J3 — Should FlowAI-on-FlowAI (the platform improving its own UI/source) be the PRIMARY proof-of-concept — i.e., fix the product's ability to improve itself BEFORE testing any external product (RelTwin, SAIGE, etc.) — per CA-18 §5 ("FlowAI applies to its own development process")?

options.text: YES, self-first. §5 explicitly makes FlowAI-on-FlowAI canonical. A platform that cannot improve itself through its own UI has not yet demonstrated the §1 promise; testing external products before the self-test is theatre. Lock external proof until self-loop closes.

No — self-loop and external-loop should proceed in parallel. Self-loop matures the engine; external-loop matures the I/O surface (jurisdictional declarations, deploy-target diversity, finding-source breadth). Each surfaces different defects.

No — external products are higher fidelity proofs. FlowAI itself is too small/familiar a target; improving its own static dashboard does not exercise the full §2 dimension space. RelTwin/SAIGE are richer test surfaces.

Self-first ONLY through a defined milestone (e.g. one full improvement cycle completed against flowai-dun.vercel.app/flowai with measurable score delta + new URL deployed), then external products. Avoids indefinite self-loop while honoring §5.

questions.topic: J4 — Is the current testing approach (running improvement cycles via CLI scripts invoked through Claude Code agents, with the UI unable to complete a full cycle) valid evidence that FlowAI works as a product, or does it invalidate the proof because the product is not being exercised through its own product surface?

options.text: INVALIDATES the proof. FlowAI's product surface is the UI per CA-18 §1 ("any URL in -> new deployable URL out"). Cycles run via Claude Code CLI workarounds prove only that the engine library functions, not that the product exists. A product that requires an LLM agent operator to bypass its own UI is not yet a product.

VALID as engine-level proof; INVALID as product-level proof. Distinguish the two: the CLI runs prove the §29 Construction Engine + §10 Self-Audit work end-to-end; they do not prove the product surface works. Both proofs are needed; the current state has one of two.

VALID for the proof phase. CLI/Claude-Code invocation is the same FlowAI engine; the UI is a deployment surface, not the engine. Proof-of-concept requires the engine to function; UI wiring is a downstream Ship-engineering task. Do not conflate the two.

Worse than invalid — actively misleading. Reporting "FlowAI improved product X" when the only invocation path was a Claude-Code-operated CLI builds false expectations among reviewers/stakeholders that the UI works. Either (a) stop calling these runs "FlowAI improvement cycles" until the UI closes the loop, or (b) explicitly mark every artifact "produced via CLI; UI does not yet support this".
